object_description: long flat volume set into the slope edge, three storeys above the yard and five on the valley side
design_condition: the long flat building is positioned as an architectural formulation of the slope edge between the upper playground and the lower sports area, its section absorbing the level difference

positive: The design cleverly plays with the existing slope edge between the playground above and the sports area below
The long flat building formulates the slope edge and extends the grove
The volume is only three storeys above ground towards the playground and five on the valley side, in consideration of the historic wing
The schoolyard is clearly defined and the space behind the existing wing is integrated as an open space sequence
The patio set into the schoolyard supports the idea of the building on the slope edge and makes the mezzanine identity recognisable
Attractive spatial references and transparency into the landscape behind are achieved
The height of the more public level places the two site levels in relation to each other again
The upper level groups sequences of play and learning spaces for different age groups around the playground
The lower green space is extended as a sports park, ensuring a gentle transition to the landscape
Restrained use of that part of the site leaves long-term potential for future extensions
Simple direct staircases connect the different entrances and levels pragmatically
The compact building develops its own dominance without unduly impairing the historic wing
Precise positioning and strong horizontal facade accentuation let the stately historic wing continue to appear dominant
Extensive transparency of the ground and mezzanine floors divides and structures the volumes and facades in many layers
The balcony layer accentuates horizontality and makes interiors appear more spacious and the school more transparent
The authors intervene subtly in the substance of the two existing wings
The generously dimensioned corridor and studio zone offers a great deal of flexibility in use
The entrance hall with a skylight set into the floor connects the mezzanine, offering varied outdoor spaces and uses
The spectator gallery is cleverly arranged at ground level on the valley side, forming an attractive spatial context
Two storey-high steel trusses divide the mezzanine into three column-free zones for the large-format rooms
A clear structural system follows the architectural and functional logic and promises efficient load transfer
High formal and spatial consistency, with the mezzanine idea determining the layering of uses and the structural concept
The open space concept impresses with clear zoning and careful handling of existing qualities
negative: The length of the building sets its north-east corner back from the forest
The woodland planting knits the existing structures somewhat timidly
The main access from the street has not been upgraded and the street space is not convincing
Too little consideration is given to the necessary obstacle-free access in the existing wings
The combined cluster and workroom arrangement cannot satisfactorily guarantee the desired school within the school
The envisaged flexibility is unlikely to be easy to solve, as the workrooms need a separate fire compartment
The required building depth brings the lower storeys very close to the protected wing and leads to complex excavation support
Missing gymnasium areas during construction have a negative impact on the phasing
The project has above-average floor area and volume figures and therefore above-average total costs
Large differences in area compared to the spatial programme negatively affect overall costs
The proximity of the new wing to the protected wing has been reached above ground and exceeded below ground
